div.head: CHn cor 8.1
div.ab: Quodsi perfidiæ uel sceleris conuictus fuerit, sicut iustum fuerit, sic emendet.
Quodsi perfidiae vel sceleris convictus fuerit, sicut iustum fuerit sic emendet.
But if he has been convicted of treason or felony, he shall make amends as has been established by law.
div.note: Added October 2026 from Robertson pp. 280–281 (text and translation); Liebermann’s text added from Gesetze I p. 522, October 2026 (two independent readings of the page images)

note.seg: erit culpa statt i. f. Alb
erit culpa instead of i. f. Alb

Unter perfidia vel scelus sehen treason bzw. felony Pol Mai II 512. Jedenfalls ist hier eine über schwerste Geldstrafe hinausgehende Strafe, also Leibesstrafe, gemeint. Vgl. Gl Verbrechen 2A. Vielleicht trat damals noch, gemäss Wilhelms I. Einführung, Verstümmelung statt Todes ein; als neue lex verzeichnet das Hängen des handhaften Diebes erst wieder zu 1108 Flor. Wig.

Pol Mai II 512 see in perfidia vel scelus treason and felony respectively. In any case a punishment going beyond the heaviest money penalty, i.e. corporal punishment, is meant here. Cf. Gl Verbrechen 2A. Perhaps at that time, in accordance with William I’s innovation, mutilation was still imposed instead of death; Flor. Wig. records the hanging of the thief caught in the act as a new lex only again under 1108
